title: Async embedding backfill: concurrency cap, retries, index matching
scenario: An asyncio client batches documents to a mock embeddings endpoint behind a semaphore, retries transient errors with Retry-After/backoff, matches response items by index, and summarises norms and token usage.

verified.why_correct: Header names are lower-cased before the lookup, so 'Retry-After' is found whatever the case; float() accepts the fractional '0.3'; and backoff_s * 2 ** attempt with attempt starting at 0 is exactly the README formula (0.05, then 0.1).
urlopen raises HTTPError for 4xx/5xx; catching it and returning a Response with err.code keeps the status for the retry logic instead of turning it into an exception.

bugs.title: datetime serialised with str()
bugs.symptom: Test 1 test_request_body: metadata.newest_update is '2026-04-03 08:15:00' instead of '2026-04-03T08:15:00'. Everything else in the body matches.
bugs.why: str(datetime) uses a space between date and time ('2026-04-03 08:15:00'), not the ISO 8601 'T' form the README requires for newest_update.
hints: Compare the newest_update the server received with the README example character by character.
json.dumps can't encode datetime itself. Look at the `default` hook passed in encode_body.
probes: Why does json.dumps need a default hook at all here?
What would happen if newest_update were a date instead of a datetime?

bugs.title: Fresh semaphore per batch
bugs.symptom: Test 1 test_concurrency_limit: '7 not less than or equal to 2'. The server saw all 7 batches in flight at once. All results are unchanged.
bugs.why: Each call builds its own semaphore, so every batch acquires a private one immediately. The shared self._limit is created but never used, and all 7 batches hit the server at once.
hints: The server saw more than 2 requests at the same time. What is supposed to cap that?
Find where a semaphore is acquired in client.py, and which semaphore it is.
Use the shared `async with self._limit:` created in __init__.
probes: Why didn't any result change when the cap was missing?
Why must the semaphore wrap the whole retry loop, not just one attempt?

bugs.title: Retry loop one attempt short
bugs.symptom: Test 2 test_attempts_per_batch: b04 gets 2 attempts (server-side and reported) instead of 3. Its final status is still failed/503.
bugs.why: max_retries counts retries, so there are max_retries + 1 attempts. range(max_retries) stops after 2 attempts for b04, which always returns 503.
hints: b04 always gets 503. How many times should it be tried with max_retries = 2?
Look at the loop bounds in send_with_retries.
probes: Why did b02 and b06 still succeed with one attempt fewer?
With the short loop, what does the last iteration do after b04's final 503?

bugs.title: Backoff sleep not awaited
bugs.symptom: Test 2 test_retry_after_respected: the two b02 requests are about 0.09 s apart ('0.09 not greater than or equal to 0.3'). A 'coroutine ... was never awaited' RuntimeWarning is printed.
bugs.why: Calling asyncio.sleep() without await only creates a coroutine object, which is thrown away; nothing waits, so b02 is retried right after the 429 despite Retry-After: 0.3. Python logs 'coroutine ... was never awaited'.
hints: The two b02 requests are less than 0.3 s apart. Did the client wait at all?
Run the tests and read the warnings. Then look at the sleep in send_with_retries.
probes: Why didn't the missing wait change the number of attempts or the final status?
Why is time.sleep() the wrong fix inside a coroutine?

bugs.title: Embeddings matched by position
bugs.old:
for item in response.body["data"]:
            doc = batch["docs"][item["index"]]
bugs.new: for doc, item in zip(batch["docs"], response.body["data"]):
bugs.symptom: Test 3 test_doc_norms: sup-01 shows 10.77 and sup-04 shows 6.403 (swapped). sup-03 and every other document are correct.
bugs.why: zip pairs documents with items by position, but the README says items can arrive in any order and must be matched by their `index` field. b03's items come back reversed, so sup-01 and sup-04 swap vectors.
hints: sup-01 and sup-04 have each other's norms. What is special about batch b03?
Look at how _outcome assigns each response item to a document.
Use doc = batch['docs'][item['index']] instead of zipping by position.
probes: Why did sup-03 come out right anyway?

bugs.title: tokens_per_doc floor-divided
bugs.old: "tokens_per_doc": round(total_tokens / len(embedded), 2) if embedded else None,
bugs.new: "tokens_per_doc": round(total_tokens // len(embedded), 2) if embedded else None,
bugs.symptom: Test 3 test_summary: tokens_per_doc is 6 instead of 6.93. The other summary fields match.
bugs.why: // is floor division, so 104 / 15 = 6.93 becomes 6 before rounding.
hints: tokens_per_doc is a whole number. Should it be?
Look at how summarize computes it.
probes: Why does round(…, 2) not save you here?
Which input would make the two versions agree?

context_qa.a: It runs run_backfill with asyncio.run: load_config, load_documents, make_batches, then EmbeddingClient.embed_all, which gathers embed_batch for every batch. The outcomes are turned into the batches and docs dicts, and summarize builds the summary.

context_qa.q: How does a request reach the server?
context_qa.a: embed_batch encodes the body with payloads.encode_body (json.dumps with a default hook for datetimes), then calls send_with_retries with a lambda that awaits transport.post. post runs the blocking send_sync in a worker thread via asyncio.to_thread.
A tuple (last Response, number of attempts). It stops at the first status outside TRANSIENT, or when the attempt counter reaches max_retries, and sleeps for retry_delay(...) between attempts.

context_qa.q: What does the mock server do for each batch id?
context_qa.a: SCRIPT in tests/mock_server.py: b01/b07 succeed, b02 gets 429 with Retry-After 0.3 and then 200, b03 succeeds with its data items reversed, b04 always returns 503, b05 returns 400, b06 returns 500 and then 200. Every request takes about 0.08 s and the server tracks max_in_flight.

context_qa.q: Where is the concurrency limit set up?
context_qa.a: EmbeddingClient.__init__ creates self._limit = asyncio.Semaphore(config.max_concurrency); config.json sets max_concurrency to 2. embed_batch acquires a semaphore around the call to send_with_retries.

context_qa.q: How is a document's norm computed?
context_qa.a: client.vector_norm takes the square root of the sum of squared components and rounds to 3 decimals. build_report applies it to the vector stored for each doc id in the outcome's `vectors` dict.
summarize adds up outcome['tokens'] (usage.total_tokens for ok batches, 0 for failed ones) and divides by the number of embedded documents, rounded to 2 decimals.
